quick: 1 h before or 2 h after food
Reduce to once daily if CrCl <=30 mL/min
Renal function, signs of tendon/CNS effects
summary: Norfloxacin is a fluoroquinolone concentrating in the urinary tract, used for uncomplicated and complicated UTIs, prostatitis and uncomplicated gonorrhea. Usual adult dose is 400 mg twice daily on an empty stomach. As a fluoroquinolone it carries class warnings for tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, QT prolongation and aortic aneurysm; reserve for infections without alternative options.
indications: Uncomplicated urethral and cervical gonorrhea (where susceptible)

dosage.n: 3 days (E. coli/most); 7-10 days for other organisms

admin: Take with a glass of water 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals
Separate from antacids, sucralfate, iron/zinc and dairy by at least 2 hours
Maintain adequate hydration to prevent crystalluria
Complete the full course even if symptoms improve
moa: Norfloxacin inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, enzymes essential for DNA replication, transcription, repair and recombination, causing rapid bactericidal killing of susceptible Gram-negative and some Gram-positive organisms.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to norfloxacin or other quinolones
History of tendon disorders related to quinolone use

preg: Avoid in pregnancy; fluoroquinolones may affect developing cartilage in animal studies. Use only if there is no safer alternative and benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Norfloxacin is not recommended during breastfeeding because of potential effects on the infant's joints and cartilage.
renal: Reduce dosing frequency to 400 mg once daily when creatinine clearance is 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 or lower. Maintain hydration to avoid crystalluria.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment defined; use with caution in significant hepatic impairment.

major: Class III/IA antiarrhythmics and other QT-prolonging drugs - additive QT prolongation
Theophylline - raised theophylline levels and toxicity
moderate: Corticosteroids - increased tendon rupture risk in elderly
minor: Probenecid - reduced renal excretion of norfloxacin
interactions.food: Multivalent cations (antacids, dairy, iron, zinc, sucralfate) chelate norfloxacin and reduce absorption - separate by 2 hours.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; may worsen dizziness and CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause crystalluria and transient rises in liver enzymes/creatinine.

monitoring: Renal function, especially in the elderly and dehydrated
Signs of tendon pain/swelling, neuropathy and CNS effects
ECG/QTc if cardiac risk factors or QT-prolonging co-medication
counsel: Take on an empty stomach with plenty of water and finish the whole course
Separate antacids, dairy, iron and zinc by at least 2 hours
Stop and seek care for tendon pain/swelling, numbness/tingling, or palpitations
Avoid prolonged sun exposure and report severe diarrhea
Avoid alcohol and driving if dizzy
pk: Bactericidal within hours; urine levels high
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F), protect from light
pearls: Concentrates in urinary tract - mainly a UTI/prostatitis agent, not for systemic infections
Fluoroquinolone class warnings: tendon rupture, neuropathy, CNS effects, QT prolongation, aortic aneurysm
High and rising gonococcal fluoroquinolone resistance limits its use in gonorrhea
Separate from cations (antacids, dairy, iron) to preserve absorption
Reserve for when other antibiotics are unsuitable, especially in elderly with tendon/aortic risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not double up. Complete the full prescribed course.
overdose: No specific antidote. Maintain adequate hydration and observe for CNS effects and crystalluria; treat symptomatically. Hemodialysis removes only a small fraction of the drug.
